flashcard_questions.a: The three elements a business balances when it designs a product.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the cost element of the design mix consider?
flashcard_questions.a: How much it costs to manufacture the product.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a unique selling point?
flashcard_questions.a: A feature that makes a product different from and better than competing products.
Actions a business takes to lengthen a product's life and prevent decline.
The complete range of products and services a business offers its customers.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens to sales at the maturity stage of the product life cycle?
flashcard_questions.a: They reach their peak and the market becomes saturated.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens to sales at the introduction stage of the product life cycle?
flashcard_questions.a: They are low, because customers are not yet aware of the product.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is the research and development stage expensive for a business?
flashcard_questions.a: Money is spent with no revenue coming in.

flashcard_questions.q: Name the extension strategy Uncle Ben's rice used when it became Ben's Original.
Which extension strategy did Netflix use when it moved from film enthusiasts to families?
How many generations of the VW Golf have appeared since 1974?
Which smartphone brand was withdrawn in 2016 after touchscreen phones overtook it?
Which sports car set a production-car record of 268 mph in 2010?
Which element of the design mix does Apple's iPhone prioritise?
What is Amazon's unique selling point for Prime members?

notes: 15 cards: 5 term→definition (design mix, cost element, USP, extension strategies, product mix), 3 life-cycle stage cards, 7 concept→named example with the lesson's own figures (Ben's Original, Netflix, VW Golf eight generations, BlackBerry 2016, Bugatti 268 mph, iPhone aesthetics, Amazon Prime). The seven differentiation routes were not turned into one list card — that would be an enumeration answer.
